column2: Retain hearing, tearing his own garments, putting on sackcloth and entering the Lord's house. The order of Hezekiah's response remains explicit.
Retain the steward, scribe and priestly elders in sackcloth, sent to Isaiah son of Amos. The clothing applies to the delegation rather than being moved to Isaiah.

Retain affliction, rebuke and provocation, followed by children reaching birth pains and the mother's lack of strength. The image is not silently replaced with children reaching an anatomical opening.

Reorder Rhapsakes's words to the words of Rhapsakes so that whom clearly identifies the person sent, not the words. Preserve the uncertain perhaps, all, living God, blasphemous words and prayer for the existing remnant. The imperative prayer request renders the future instruction contextually; the close draft retains the inherited order.
Retain the arrival of Hezekiah's servants at Isaiah after the reported message. This repeated arrival is not rearranged to reconstruct chronology.
Retain the nested message to the human master, the Lord's prohibition of fear and the Assyrian king's young servants as the blaspheming agents. No explicit Me is inserted as the object of blasphemy.

Retain behold, present giving of a spirit, hearing a report, return to his own land and being brought down by the sword there. Spirit remains indefinite and does not predetermine a personal spirit or inward disposition.
Retain Rhapsakes's return, fighting at Lomna and departure from Lachish. The two he references preserve the compressed report without claiming that both refer to one person.

Retain Tharaka king of the Ethiopians, the report of his emergence to fight and the return-and-send sequence. Returned is not silently reduced to again; the hearing and sending subject is contextually the Assyrian king but remains unexpressed.
column3: How should the change of subject from Rhapsakes to the Assyrian king be made audible without over-resolving the syntax?

column2: Retain the hostile warning that the trusted God should not lift Hezekiah up, and the emphatic non-surrender quotation. Ordinary you addresses the king; capitalization identifies the reported deity without endorsing the taunt.

Retain behold, everything, all lands, destruction under the ban and the incredulous rescue question. Devoting to destruction expresses the contextual force of anathematize rather than a general curse alone.

Retain the gods/nations question, ancestral destroyers and Gozan, Charran, Raphes and sons of Edem in Thaesthen. The English attaches destroyed to nations contextually; the Greek relative and subsequent place list require syntactic review.
column3: Does the relative clause refer grammatically to the nations' gods or collectively to the named populations and places?

column2: Retain the kings of Aimath and Arphad and the subsequent bare place names Seppharouain, Ana and Ava. No repeated king is supplied for the latter list.

Retain plural letters, taking and reading them, ascent to the Lord's house and unfolding before Him. Hezekiah's repeated name remains; the documents are not made a singular letter from a parallel version.
Retain direct singular divine Thou, the cherubim seat, exclusive God among all kingdoms and creation of heaven and earth. Alone is explicit; madest remains the established divine-address inflection.
Retain singular ear and plural eyes, repeated Lord, hearing, seeing and hearing again, and Sennacherib's sent words. The second hearing is not removed as redundant.
Retain the assertion that Assyrian kings truly devastated the nations. This unit continues grammatically into the following verse; no full-stop closure or additional lands is supplied.

Retain putting the gods into fire, the explanation that they are human-made wood and stones and their destruction. Human hands remains concrete, and the negation concerns their godhood within Hezekiah's prayer.
Retain the rescue petition, his singular hand, all earthly kingdoms and Thou as the only God. This concludes the prayer without changing the future knowing into an explicit purpose clause.

Replace what you did pray with what you prayed, using ordinary past tense in the Lord's address to Hezekiah. Retain Lord, God of hosts and Israel's God, and the hearing response. No archaic second-person construction is required for a human addressee.

Retain the introductory word and the parallel Zion/Jerusalem daughters, contempt, mockery and head-shaking. Proposed display lines separate the paired images without changing wording; present English depicts the enacted taunt while the Greek verbs are aorist.
column3: Would past tense better preserve the temporal relation of these aorists in the oracle?

column2: Retain the reproach/blasphemy question, raised voice and high eyes directed against Israel's Holy One. Display separates the questions and climax; neither whom nor against whom becomes a supplied divine title until the final clause.

Replace did reproach and did say with reproached and said in ordinary human address. Retain the boast's future ascent, past cutting and arrival, Lebanon's flanks, cedar height, selected cypresses and opaque melon/Carmel phrase. Display separates framing speech and boast while the close draft preserves inherited wording.
column3: What does melon designate, and how do farthest part and woodland of its Carmel depend on it? No reconstruction is accepted here.

column2: Retain cooled, foreign waters, foot's tread and all rivers of enclosure. These selected readings are not changed to dug, Egyptian rivers or a familiar parallel. Display distinguishes the paired first-person claims.
column3: What contextual sense is intended by cooled and rivers of enclosure in this edition?

column2: Retain the abrupt I formed it, now I brought it and the compressed exile/fighting-men/fortified-cities clause. Display exposes the clause breaks without supplying an absent have you not heard or ancient-time introduction.
column3: How should elevations or carryings-away, deportations, fighting men and fortified cities be construed together? The inherited wording remains unresolved.

column2: Retain weak hands, cowering, shame and the grass/herbage/rooftop-grass/trampling sequence. Display follows the successive images; the final one standing is not converted to an inferred crop-growth stage.
column3: What is the force and referent of the final standing participle in the trampling image?

column2: Retain the divine knowledge of sitting, exit, entrance and anger. Display groups the movements and anger without reversing exit and entrance; ordinary your addresses the Assyrian king.

Retain anger, arrogance reaching the ears, plural hooks in nostrils, one bridle in lips and return by the arrival road. Display separates cause, restraint and return; no nose-ring or mouth substitution obscures the selected anatomy and number.

Retain the first two years' spontaneous growth, the third year's nominal sowing/harvest/planting and the fruit. Display preserves the sequence; the final eating is plural while the initial sign and eating address the individual recipient.
column3: How should the shift of addressee from Assyria's king to the promised sign's recipient be signalled without inserting a name into the oracle?

column2: Retain the surviving remnant's root below and fruit above, with again grounded in the add/continue verb. Two display lines bring out the directional parallel without adding a new metaphor.

Retain Jerusalem's remnant, the singular escaping one from Zion and the Lord of hosts' zeal. Display pairs the locations and separates the concluding divine agency without normalizing singular escape to a plural population noun.
Retain Not so, the Lord's declaration, no entrance or arrow, the shield as grammatical subject and emphatic absence of a siege ramp. No shield-bearing troops are inserted into the selected clause.
Retain return by the same road and repeated refusal of entry, ending in says the Lord. The repetition confirms the preceding prohibition rather than supplying a second route.
Retain the Lord's shielding, His own sake and David His servant. No separately expressed save infinitive is added to this shorter selected sentence.

Remove the second they from behold, they were all dead bodies: behold, all were dead bodies preserves the Greek nominal observation without explicitly equating its subject with those who rose. Retain by night, the angel and one hundred eighty-five thousand; the close draft keeps inherited wording.
column3: Who are the unexpressed morning risers, and what is the precise scope of all in the following observation?

column2: Retain departure, going, return and residence in Nineveh. The movement verbs remain rather than collapsing them into a single flight claim.

Retain worship in Neserach's house, sons Adramelech and Sarasar as attackers, escape to Ararat and Asordan's succession. Neither the deity's name nor the royal names are silently normalized to a different textual form.
